tex_content.html:
Theorem
[Existence of approximate solutions] ↗ def:fundamental-solution-heat-equation 1. ch7:7.3-thm-1\group Hyperbolic Systems

For each $\epsilon > 0$, there exists a unique solution $\mathbf{u}^\epsilon $ of (11), with \[ \mathbf{u}^\epsilon \in L^2(0,T; H^3(\mathbb {R}^n; \mathbb {R}^m)), \quad (\mathbf{u}^\epsilon )' \in L^2(0,T; H^1(\mathbb {R}^n; \mathbb {R}^m)). \tag {12} \]

Proof

\sketch Add the viscosity term $-\varepsilon \Delta u^{\varepsilon }$ with compatible boundary data. The resulting uniformly parabolic system has a smooth solution by the parabolic existence theory.

□
